correctness.rationale: The arclength monomial norms give the stated Laurent series, and pairing the half-integers gives the Jacobi cn Fourier series with nome e^(−h) and parameter m, not modulus m. The radial operator is (1/4)∂²/∂u²; the affine prefactor of the kernel has no effect. For α=2K(m)/π the cn differential equation and initial conditions give C″=α²[(1−2m)C+2mC³] and (C′)²=α²(C²−1)(mC²+1−m), proving the log-derivative identity. The reciprocal complementary cn increases from 1 to infinity as u traverses [0,h/2); thus y=C² covers [1,∞), and the constrained minimum of my+(1−m)/y decides all radii without a cutoff. Monotonicity of K(1−m)/K(m) gives the threshold at m=1/2, h=π. Inverting complementary cn gives the advertised radius, and y−1=α²u²+O(u⁴) gives the critical coefficient α⁶/8=8K(1/2)⁶/π⁶. The central maximum beyond threshold is radial, not pointwise strict along the central circle. Independent direct Laurent variance checks at 16 interior points and a critical divided difference corroborated the proof (python3 /workspace/evidence/review_checks.py 1); the exact argument establishes the universal claims.
